title: RGCN tasks: node classification & link prediction
blurb: Final-layer prediction, negative sampling, Hits@k, reciprocal rank

hook.title: Ranking the suspects
hook.text: Link prediction in a knowledge graph is a *line-up*. For the question “Who does E have relation $r_3$ with?”, the model scores a **suspect list**: the true answer plus some impostors. Training teaches it to score the real edge high and a made-up impostor low. At evaluation we line up the true answer among *all non-training impostors* and check its **rank**. A rank of 1 is perfect; a rank of 3 means two impostors outscored it.
hook.recall: Remember the line-up: negatives are made-up edges that are *not* real (training) edges; evaluation checks the *rank* of the true edge: Hits@$k$ asks if it’s in the top $k$, reciprocal rank is $1/RK$.

explore.intro: Validation edge $(E,r_3,D)$ with negatives $(E,r_3,B)$ and $(E,r_3,F)$. Set the model’s scores.
tasks: Make the true edge rank 1, then rank 2, then rank 3. How do Hits@2 and reciprocal rank change?
Why are A and C not in the candidate list?
explore.takeaway: Score $f_r(h_E^{(L)},h_A^{(L)})=(h_E^{(L)})^\top W_rh_A^{(L)}$; loss $\ell=-\log\sigma(f_{r_3}(h_E,h_A))-\log(1-\sigma(f_{r_3}(h_E,h_B)))$; Hits@$k=\mathbb 1[RK\le k]$; reciprocal rank $=1/RK$.

items: Use RGCN to score the training supervision edge $(E,r_3,A)$
Create a negative edge by perturbing it, e.g. $(E,r_3,B)$
Use the RGCN model to score the negative edge
Optimise a standard cross-entropy: maximise the supervision-edge score, minimise the negative-edge score

questions.prompt: For node classification into $K$ classes, RGCN uses:
questions.explanation: Each entry represents the probability of a class.

questions.prompt: Training supervision edge $(E,r_3,A)$; training message edges include $(E,r_3,C)$. Which is a valid **negative** edge?
questions.explanation: “Negative edges should NOT belong to training/supervision edges: e.g. $(E,r_3,C)$ is NOT a negative edge.”

questions.prompt: Validation edge $(E,r_3,D)$ is ranked above $(E,r_3,F)$ but below $(E,r_3,B)$. What is its rank $RK$?
With $RK=2$, what is the reciprocal rank $1/RK$?
Which statement about Hits@$k$ and reciprocal rank is FALSE?
options: For both metrics higher is better
Hits@$k$ is larger when the true edge has a larger rank number
questions.explanation: A larger rank number (worse position) makes Hits@k fall to 0.

questions.prompt: Why are $(E,r_3,A)$ and $(E,r_3,C)$ excluded from the evaluation candidates for $(E,r_3,D)$?
options: They belong to training message/supervision edges
They are positive for another relation
questions.explanation: They are real training edges, not valid negatives.
